lines.japanese: 「あれ、隼人君どこ行こーとしてんの？」
lines.english: “Wait, where are you going, Hayato?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　漫喫だろ？　あそこに看板あんじゃん、あのビルだろ」
lines.english: “Huh? The comic-book café. The sign’s right there. It’s that building, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「ムリムリ、そこはムリ。寝てるおっちゃんのイビキとかカップルの喘ぎ声とか聞こえるし、トイレ和式とかありえんでしょ」
lines.english: “No, no, that place is impossible. You can hear old men snoring and couples moaning, and a squat toilet? No way.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと値段は上だけど、あっちの店のが広いし綺麗だし、飲みホの種類いっぱいあるし、あとシートも結構ふかふかだよ」
lines.english: “The place over there costs a little more, but it's bigger and cleaner, the drink bar has a huge selection, and the seats are pretty plush.”

lines.japanese: 「マジで。結構ふかふかなの。具体的に言うとソレどんぐらいふかふかなの」
lines.english: “Seriously? Pretty plush? In concrete terms, how plush is *pretty plush*?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、そだねー、結構ふかふかだったと思うよー」
lines.english: “Hmm. Let's see. I remember them being pretty plush.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなか。すげえな。結構ふかふかッつったらオマエ、案外ふかふかとか比較的ふかふかよりも結構ふかふかッつうことじゃん。どんだけだよ。どんだけふかふかなの」
lines.english: “That plush? Incredible. If they're *pretty* plush, that means they're plusher than *fairly* plush or *comparatively* plush. How plush are we talking?”

lines.japanese: 「まー、言葉じゃ説明しにくいけど結構ふかふかってカンジ？」
lines.english: “Well, it's hard to put into words. They're just, you know... pretty plush?”

lines.japanese: 俺たちはボキャ貧なふかふかトークを交わしながら漫画喫茶へ向かった。
lines.english: We headed to the comic-book café, still talking about plushness with a vocabulary of about one word.

lines.japanese: 「いらっしゃいませ。当店の会員カードはお持ちですか？」
lines.english: “Welcome. Do you have a membership card with us?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なにソレ。これじゃ駄目なの」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that? This won't do?”

lines.japanese: 「隼人君、私持ってるから」
lines.english: “Hayato, I've got one.”

lines.japanese: 財布からモンキホーテのポイントカードを出しかけたところで止められた。
lines.english: She stopped me just as I was about to pull a Monki Hote points card from my wallet.

lines.japanese: なんたらシートやら、ほにゃらら席やら、ブースにもいくつか種類があるらしい。よく分からないから受付は香田に任せた。
lines.english: Apparently the booths came in several varieties: something-or-other seats and whatchamacallit rooms. I had no idea what any of it meant, so I left reception to Koda.

lines.japanese: 「すんません。この店の椅子、どんぐらいふかふかなんすか」
lines.english: “Excuse me. How plush are the chairs here?”

lines.japanese: 「そうですね、結構ふかふかだと思いますよ」
lines.english: “Let's see. I'd say they're pretty plush.”

lines.japanese: 「隼人君、こっちー。１３・１４だってー」
lines.english: “Hayato, over here. We got thirteen and fourteen.”

lines.japanese: 「１３番と１４番も結構ふかふかなんすか」
lines.english: “Are thirteen and fourteen pretty plush too?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、どの席も結構ふかふかですよ」
lines.english: “Yes. All our seats are pretty plush.”

lines.japanese: 「隼人君はやくー！　ふかふかしぼんじゃうよー！」
lines.english: “Hayato, hurry! The plushness is going flat!”

lines.japanese: 「マジで！？」
lines.english: “Seriously?!”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: なにやらミーハーそうな音楽が鳴りはじめた。香田があわててバッグをあさる。
lines.english: Some trendy-sounding music began to play. Koda hurriedly rummaged through her bag.

lines.japanese: 「んー、なにもー、こんなときにー……あ、ごめんね隼人君？」
lines.english: “Oh, come on. Why now...? Ah, sorry, Hayato?”

lines.japanese: 亜衣はケータイの画面に不平を落としたあと、俺の機嫌をうかがうように苦笑した。いちいち電話ぐらい気にしなくていいのに。どんだけ心の狭い男だと思われてんだ。
lines.english: Ai complained at the phone's screen, then gave me a strained smile as if checking my mood. She didn't have to worry about one phone call. How petty did she think I was?

lines.japanese: 「俺そのへん見てるわ」
lines.english: “I'll look around over here.”

lines.japanese: カウンター脇の案内図を見ながら言った。やつはゴメンとかすぐ切るとか言いながら、フロアの端へ寄った。
lines.english: I said it while studying the floor guide beside the counter. She moved to the edge of the room, saying sorry and promising to be quick.

lines.japanese: 「もしー？　なに？」
lines.english: “Hello? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「いま？　駅前。ネットカフェ。そーそー、あの結構ふかふかの」
lines.english: “Right now? By the station. At an internet café. Yeah, the pretty plush one.”

lines.japanese: 「ボウリング？　今から？　あーごめん、今日はムリだー」
lines.english: “Bowling? Right now? Oh, sorry. I can't today.”

lines.japanese: なんだ、友達から誘われてンのか。だったら行きゃいいのに。つうか行けよ。言いたかったけど、会話に耳を傾けていたと思われたら嫌だから言わないでおいた。
lines.english: Oh, her friends were inviting her out. Then she should go. In fact, go. I wanted to say it, but then she'd know I'd been listening, so I kept quiet.

lines.japanese: 俺はこれ以上やつの声を聞かないで済むよう、店員にどうでもいい質問を投げかけた。
lines.english: To spare myself any more of her conversation, I lobbed a meaningless question at the clerk.

lines.japanese: 「すんません、この、和室ってどーゆーことすか」
lines.english: “Excuse me. What's this ‘Japanese room’ supposed to be?”

lines.japanese: 「畳敷きのフラットシートなんです。足も伸ばせますし、仮眠にはソファー席より向いてますよ」
lines.english: “It's a flat booth with tatami flooring. You can stretch out your legs, and it's better for a nap than a sofa booth.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そういうことじゃなくてさ。ふかふかじゃないの」
lines.english: “No, that's not what I mean. It isn't plush?”

lines.japanese: 「そうですね、ソファーではなく畳になってますから、ちょっとふかふかというわけには……」
lines.english: “Well, it's tatami rather than a sofa, so I couldn't exactly call it plush...”

lines.japanese: 「まじで。はあ、そうなんだ。それはちょっとヘコむな」
lines.english: “Seriously? Huh. I see. That’s a bit of a letdown.”

lines.japanese: 「ほんとごめん！　こんど誘ってくれれば行くし、でもマジ、今日～はもう無理だから」
lines.english: “I'm really sorry! Ask me next time and I'll go, but I seriously can't todaaay.”

lines.japanese: 「てゆかカズ君、いまバニィ君らといるんでしょ？　じゃあいいじゃん。うん、そゆことで、とりあえず切るよ？」
lines.english: “Besides, Kazu, you're with Banny and the others, right? Then you're fine. Yeah. Anyway, I'm hanging up, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「あんさ、結構ふかふかじゃなくて、割合ふかふかぐらいでもいいんだけど。どうなの。やっぱ畳でふかふかは無理なの」
lines.english: “Listen, it doesn't have to be *pretty* plush. *Moderately* plush would do. What do you think? Is plushness simply impossible with tatami?”

lines.japanese: 「え……あ、聞こえた？　うん、そー、いま隼人君いっしょ。うん。や、偶然偶然、そーゆー流れで」
lines.english: “What...? Oh, you heard? Yeah, I'm with Hayato. Right. We just ran into each other, and one thing led to another.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そんなカンジだから、ゴメン、みんなによろしく言っといて。うん、じゃねー、ばいっすー」
lines.english: “Yeah, that's the situation. Sorry. Say hi to everyone for me. Okay, bye now.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅ、おまたせー！」
lines.english: “Whew. Thanks for waiting!”

lines.japanese: 「なに。友達」
lines.english: “What, was that a friend?”

lines.japanese: 森里の名前は聞こえていたけど、マナーとしてすっとぼけて訊いてみた。
lines.english: I had heard Morisato's name, but out of courtesy I played dumb and asked.

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ、そんな感じ」
lines.english: “Yeah. Something like that.”

lines.japanese: どんな感じだよ。言えよ。フツーに森里の名前言えよ。そこで伏せンの、不自然じゃねーか。
lines.english: What kind of answer was that? Say it. Just say Morisato's name. Hiding it now was unnatural.

lines.japanese: 俺は気が滅入った。おいおいおい、冗談じゃねえぞ。まさか青い春に巻きこまれてンじゃねーだろうな。
lines.english: My spirits sank. Hey, hey, this wasn’t funny. Don’t tell me I’d been dragged into some teenage romance.

lines.japanese: 言っとくけど、青春小僧たちの和を乱すなんて御免だからな。俺はお気楽な学生諸君と違って、ニッポン経済を支える小さい歯車のひとつなんだ。ままごと恋愛なんかとっくに卒業してる。
lines.english: For the record, I wasn’t about to stir up trouble among you lovesick kids. Unlike you carefree students, I was one tiny cog keeping the Japanese economy turning. I’d outgrown make-believe romance ages ago.

lines.japanese: 「森里？」
lines.english: “Morisato?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、うん」
lines.english: “Oh. Yeah.”

lines.japanese: だろ。森里だろ。最初から言っとけよ、そう。
lines.english: Exactly. Morisato. You should've said so from the start.

lines.japanese: 「みんなで一緒にいるから、カズ君が代表で電話くれたみたい」
lines.english: “Everyone's together, so I guess Kazu called on their behalf.”

lines.japanese: 聞いてねえよ。なに補足説明してんだよ。べつにあのロンゲが、おまえに個人的なラブコール送ったところでなんとも思わねえよ。
lines.english: I didn't ask. Why add that explanation? I couldn't care less if that long-haired bastard had made a personal love call to you.

lines.japanese: 「カズ君も暇だよねー。幼馴染みのトコなんか電話してないで、早くカノジョでも作ればいいのに」
lines.english: “Kazu has too much time on his hands. Instead of calling his childhood friend, he should hurry up and get himself a girlfriend.”

lines.japanese: ちょ、待てよ。なんだよその説明くさいセリフ。
lines.english: Wait. What was with that suspiciously expository line?

lines.japanese: 分かってるよ。そんな、わざとらしく牽制しなくたって、おまえが森里と付きあってるわけじゃないことぐらい、もう分かってる。
lines.english: I knew. You didn't have to warn me off so pointedly. I already knew you and Morisato weren't dating.

lines.japanese: でも、おまえは相手をただの幼馴染みだと思ってるのかもしれないが、向こうはそうじゃねえぞ。あいつはおまえにピンクの矢印でてんぞ。それは俺の気が滅入る理由のひとつだ。
lines.english: But you might think he's only a childhood friend. He doesn't feel the same. There's a big pink arrow pointing straight from him to you. That was one reason my spirits had sunk.

lines.japanese: つって、俺がむっつり黙ってたら、また妙な方向で勘違いされるじゃねーか。ああ面倒くせえ。
lines.english: And if I sat there glowering in silence, she'd misunderstand me in some other bizarre direction. God, what a pain.

lines.japanese: 「よし、じゃあさっさとインターネットを始めようぜ。部屋、１３番と１４番だっけ」
lines.english: “Right. Let's hurry up and start the internet. Our rooms were thirteen and fourteen?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ペアシート取れれば良かったんだけど、もう埋まっちゃってるんだって」
lines.english: “Yeah. I wanted to get a pair booth, but they said they were all taken.”

lines.japanese: そりゃ結構。
lines.english: Excellent.

lines.japanese: 「えー、狭くたっていいじゃん、一緒に見ようよ。初めてのネットじゃ、すぐ分かんないとこ出てくるよ？　私が付いてた方がいいってー」
lines.english: “Oh, come on, who cares if it's cramped? Let's look together. This is your first time online; you'll run into something you don't understand right away. You're better off with me there.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、俺もうインターネット完璧だから。こんだけ教えてもらえばソロデビュー余裕だから」
lines.english: “No, I've already mastered the internet. With this much instruction, I'm more than ready for my solo debut.”

lines.japanese: 掲示板とやらの見方をざっと教わった俺は、騒がしい教師を隣りの個室へ追いやって、ひとりそこに並ぶ文字列を凝視していた。
lines.english: After a quick lesson in how to read this message-board thing, I banished my noisy teacher to the booth next door and stared alone at the rows of text.

lines.japanese: そして──すぐに目が疲れてきた。あと頭も。
lines.english: And before long—my eyes began to hurt. My head too.
“Whew...”

lines.japanese: もともと俺が活字とか苦手ってのは大きいけれど、それでなくとも、掲示板のやつらはヴィジュアル系気取りな言いまわしや仲間うちで流行ってるっぽい隠語を多用してて一見さんに優しくない雰囲気だ。
lines.english: I was never much of a reader, but that wasn’t the only problem. The posters wrote like members of some flamboyant rock band and peppered everything with insider slang. The place wasn’t exactly welcoming to newcomers.

lines.japanese: そもそもＲ－ウィングの母体は、ロックバードなるアマチュアバンドのファンクラブなわけだから、俺にはまったく知識も興味もない音楽ネタが話題の多くを占めている。
lines.english: R-Wing had started as the fan club of an amateur band called Rockbird, so naturally most of the discussion was music talk I neither understood nor cared about.

lines.japanese: とくに、自己破壊願望を開陳したお耽美ポエムや、ソフトめの性倒錯を綴ったセックス白書、ドラッグ嗜好を臭わせるような趣味の悪いデカダン日記は、俺の美意識からかけ離れていて反吐が出そうだった。
lines.english: Worst of all were the precious poems parading self-destructive urges, the sex reports chronicling softcore perversities, and the tasteless decadent diaries hinting at a fondness for drugs. They were so far outside my aesthetic that I felt sick.

lines.japanese: くだらねえ。
lines.english: Garbage.

lines.japanese: 香田の言うところでは「とりま、半年ぐらい前までのログが残ってるね」とのことだったが、時間も限られてることだし、俺はここ数日分の書き込みに絞りこんで目を通した。
lines.english: According to Koda, ‘Looks like the logs go back about six months or so.’ But time was short, so I narrowed my reading to posts from the last few days.

lines.japanese: そして、それは正解だったみたいだ。掲示板の雰囲気が変わってきたのは、ちょうどその辺りからだった。
lines.english: That seemed to have been the right choice. It was around then that the atmosphere of the board began to change—

lines.japanese: ──変革は、柳木原少年自警団を名乗る“敵”の出現によって。
lines.english: —with the appearance of an “enemy” calling itself the Yanagihara Youth Vigilantes.

lines.japanese: 当然っちゃ当然だけど、俺の知らないところでもＲ－ウィングと柳木原フレイムバーズは、大なり小なり数々のいさかいを起こしていたみたいだ。
lines.english: It made sense, but apparently R-Wing and the Yanagihara Flame Birds had been getting into clashes large and small without my knowing a thing about it.

lines.japanese: それまで手首や胸に可愛い傷を刻み、破滅を謳った平和な国の音楽に酔いしれ、手慰み程度の幻覚剤で宇宙の真理を知った気になっていた子供たちは、そうして暴力という新たな娯楽に愉悦を見出した。
lines.english: Until then, these children had carved pretty little wounds into their wrists and chests, swooned over music from a peaceful country as it sang of ruin, and fancied that recreational hallucinogens had shown them the truth of the universe. Now they had discovered a new amusement: violence.

lines.japanese: 何人やっただの誰々がやられただのを箇条書きで述べた文字列は、まるで大掛かりなサバイバルゲームの経過報告みたいで現実味がない。
lines.english: The strings of text listing how many they had taken out and exactly who had gone down read like progress reports from one enormous airsoft match. None of it felt real.

lines.japanese: 現実味がない──だからきっと、やつらもこんな冗談みたいな戦争ごっこを続けていられたんじゃないか。すべては憶測に過ぎないけれど。
lines.english: It didn't feel real—and perhaps that was precisely why they could keep playing at this ridiculous little war. But that was only speculation.

lines.japanese: １１月２２日。ハリュー襲撃せらるの報が投じられ、一気に書き込みの量が増える。そこには狂信的なガキ共の青臭い怒りがほとばしっていた。
lines.english: November 22. Word came that Haryu had been attacked, and the volume of posts exploded. The callow fury of fanatical children poured across the screen.

lines.japanese: １１月２３日。血走った信者たちは、聖戦の名のもと、各所でフレイムバーズの下部組織に“討ち入り”を仕掛けた。
lines.english: November 23. In the name of holy war, the bloodshot faithful launched ‘raids’ on Flame Birds affiliates all over town.

lines.japanese: その中に混じって記されていた、敵と誤認して“勇敢にして寛大なる隼”に刃物を向けた男の話に、俺は心当たりがあった。投稿者の名前は案の定「咲夜」。
lines.english: Buried among the reports was the story of a man who had mistaken someone for the enemy and drawn a blade on ‘the brave and magnanimous Falcon.’ I knew what that meant. Sure enough, the poster was named Sakuya.

lines.japanese: “隼は孤高。孤高なれば敵にあらず味方にあらず。志を近しくする同朋と見つけたり”
lines.english: *The Falcon stands alone. In solitude, neither foe nor friend. Yet in him have we found a comrade of kindred purpose.*

lines.japanese: 同朋じゃねえよ。誉めるな、俺を誉めるな。
lines.english: I'm not your comrade. Don't praise me. Stop praising me.

lines.japanese: １１月２４日。激化する戦渦。被害と憎しみの輪が広がり、いよいよ物騒なことをほざくやつも出てきた。飛び道具を手に入れたとほのめかしているのが、おそらくあのオウム頭の大司教だろう。
lines.english: November 24. The fires of war burned higher. The circles of injury and hatred spread, and at last some of them began talking about truly dangerous things. The one hinting that he'd obtained a ranged weapon was probably that parrot-headed archbishop.

lines.japanese: 投稿者名は「パトリアーク・ヨーゼフ」。覚えにくい。やっぱ大司教でいい。もしくはオウム、もしくはオカマだ。
lines.english: His screen name was Patriarch Josef. Too hard to remember. Archbishop was fine. Or Parrot. Or queen.

lines.japanese: しかし気になったのが、その飛び道具の入手経路だ。そこには「平穏を蝕む蛇蠍より奪取せり」とある。
lines.english: What did bother me was where the weapon had come from. He wrote that it had been ‘seized from the vipers and scorpions that gnaw upon our peace.’

lines.japanese: 奪取せり──つまり、その種の売人から買ったものではないらしい。あんな物騒なおもちゃ、どこのどなたから盗んだって言うんだろう。
lines.english: *Seized*—so apparently he hadn't bought it from a dealer in that kind of thing. Just who had he stolen such a dangerous toy from?

lines.japanese: 俺はマウスから手を放し、香田が俺用にと置いていったジンジャーエールで喉を潤した。
lines.english: I took my hand from the mouse and wet my throat with the ginger ale Koda had left for me.

lines.japanese: １１月２５日。ついに大司教の召集命令が下った。
lines.english: November 25. At last, the Archbishop issued the order to muster.

lines.japanese: “主の快復近し。今宵、ロックバードの再臨なるやもしれず。総員、身を濯ぎて聖地に集え”
lines.english: *Our Lord’s recovery is near. Tonight may witness the second coming of Rockbird. Let all purify themselves and gather upon the holy ground.*

lines.japanese: ここには記されていないが、もちろん俺はその後のあらましを知っている。オウムとニワトリ、親分同士の一騎打ちは前者の大敗で終わった。
lines.english: It wasn't recorded here, but of course I knew what followed. Parrot and Chicken, the two bosses, fought one on one. Parrot got demolished.

lines.japanese: 果たして翌１１月２６日。今日のことだ。不毛な戦争ごっこに幕が閉じられている。
lines.english: And so, on November 26—today—the curtain had finally fallen on their barren little war.

lines.japanese: “終戦協定、締結せり”
lines.english: An armistice hath been concluded.

lines.japanese: どうやら大司教は重傷を負って病院へ運びこまれたらしい。戦意と戦力を大きく失ったＲ－ウィングは柳木原フレイムバーズの軍門に降り、それを良しとしない者は潔くチームを去っている。
lines.english: Apparently, the archbishop had been badly wounded and taken to a hospital. With both its will and its strength broken, R-Wing had surrendered to the Yanagihara Flame Birds. Those who couldn't accept that had made a clean break and left the group.

lines.japanese: どちらにせよ、その後の掲示板には、一過性のムーブメントが過ぎたあとに残るある種の無常観が漂っていた。
lines.english: Either way, the posts that followed were steeped in the peculiar sense of transience left behind when a passing craze had run its course.

lines.japanese: たとえばペットボトルのおまけを馬鹿みたいに集めまくって、しかしふと熱が冷めたときに決まって訪れる、後悔とまでは呼べないあの気まずげな空気だ。
lines.english: It was the awkward feeling that always came after you’d collected a ridiculous mountain of freebies from bottled drinks, only to wake one day and find the fever gone—not quite regret, but close enough to make you uncomfortable.

lines.japanese: 掲示板は急速に活気を失い、以前のような訳知り顔の音楽評論だけが埋み火のようにくすぶっていた。
lines.english: The board rapidly went quiet. Only the same smug music criticism as before smoldered on like embers under ash.

lines.japanese: １７時３４分。口数の少ないたまり場に、反撃ののろしをあげよと檄が飛んだ。
lines.english: At 5:34 p.m., a fiery call for retaliation cut through the quiet of the message board.

lines.japanese: 投稿者はパトリアーク・ヨーゼフ──白いパイプベッドに横たわっているはずのオウムが、香田のように携帯端末からアクセスしたのだろうか。
lines.english: The poster was Patriarch Josef. Was the parrot who ought to have been lying in a white hospital bed logging in from a mobile device, like Koda?

lines.japanese: “我らが主の聖痕にかけて、赦されざる咎に裁きを！　紅き涙をもって朱き血を漱がん！”
lines.english: *By the stigmata of our Lord, judgment upon the unforgivable transgression! With crimson tears shall scarlet blood be cleansed!*

lines.japanese: しかしそれは、消えかかった火にわざわざ湿った焚き木を放りこんだようなものだった。
lines.english: But it was like going out of his way to throw damp firewood on a dying flame.

lines.japanese: Ｒ－ウィングの残党にとってみればフレイムバーズとの戦争ごっこはすでに終わった遊びだし、ましてや敗軍の将が兵を語るなど不快以外のなにものでもない。
lines.english: To R-Wing’s remnants, the war with the Flame Birds was a game already over. Having their defeated commander lecture them about war was more than they could stomach.

lines.japanese: 誰かが匿名でぽつりと言った。もう大司教は放置しろ。
lines.english: One anonymous poster quietly said: *Leave the Archbishop alone.*

lines.japanese: 掲示板の書き込みはそこで終わっている。
lines.english: That was where the board ended.

lines.japanese: 俺はふたたびグラスに口をつけた。
lines.english: I raised the glass to my lips again.

lines.japanese: まあ……問題はなさそうだ。
lines.english: Well... It didn't look as if there was anything to worry about.

lines.japanese: あの大司教が退院したとして、やつにはすでに仲間もいない。
lines.english: Even if the archbishop got out of the hospital, he had no comrades left.

lines.japanese: とりあえず、事態は収束したと見ていいだろう。俺は椅子の背もたれにどっかと体を預けて、一つ大きく息を吸った。リクライニングシートは結構ふかふかだ。
lines.english: For the time being, I could safely call the matter settled. I threw my weight against the chair back and drew one long breath. The reclining seat was, indeed, pretty plush.

lines.japanese: もともと連中の争いなんか俺の知ったこっちゃないが、これで完全に心配事はなくなった。
lines.english: Their squabble had never been any of my concern, but now the last of my worries was gone.

lines.japanese: 「終わった終わった」
lines.english: “Done and done.”

lines.japanese: 俺はパソコンの画面から目を離し、並んで置かれた薄っすいテレビを点ける。なんとなく音が欲しかった。
lines.english: I looked away from the computer and switched on the thin television beside it. For no particular reason, I wanted some noise.

lines.japanese: ぼうっと映りこんできた恋愛ドラマを睨みながら、グラスを傾けて喉に──
lines.english: Glaring vacantly at the romance drama that flickered into view, I tipped the glass to pour its contents down my—

lines.japanese: ──あれ、中身カラじゃねえかコノヤロウ。
lines.english: —wait, the damn thing was empty.

lines.japanese: 俺は氷だけのグラスを手にブースを出る。ちょうどさっきの店員が通りかかった。
lines.english: I left the booth carrying a glass full of nothing but ice. The same employee from earlier happened to pass by.

lines.japanese: 「すんません。あの、アレどこすか。あのホラ、あのコーラ的なもんがジャーッて出る、あの飲み放題マシーンみたいの」
lines.english: “Excuse me. Where's the, uh, thing? You know, the all-you-can-drink machine where cola stuff comes rushing out?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ドリンクサーバーですか？」
lines.english: “Oh, the drink dispenser?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、名前は知んないけど、あのウーロン茶的なもんがビャーッて出たり、コーヒー的なもんがドプヮーッて出る、あの飲み放題マシーンみたいなやつ」
lines.english: “I don't know what it's called. The all-you-can-drink machine where oolong-tea stuff goes *shwaa* and coffee stuff comes out *bworrsh*.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、お飲み物のコーナーでしたらこちらにございます」
lines.english: “Yes, sir. The beverage station is right this way.”

lines.japanese: 店員が丁寧な所作で歩きだす。俺はグラスを提げたまま付いていった。なんだか看護師さんと採尿に行く気分だ。
lines.english: The employee set off with impeccable manners. I followed with the glass dangling from my hand. Somehow it felt like a nurse was escorting me to provide a urine sample.

lines.japanese: 遊園地の巨大迷路みたいなフロアでひとつめの角を折れたとき、一瞬、視界の隅を慌ただしい影たちがよぎっていった。
lines.english: As we rounded the first corner of a floor laid out like an enormous amusement-park maze, two hurried shadows flickered at the edge of my vision.
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: なんだ、あの逃げるような動きは。男ふたり……だったよな。鬼ごっこでもしてんのか？
lines.english: What was with the way they fled? Two men... right? Were they playing tag or something?

lines.japanese: 「お客様？」
lines.english: “Sir?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、すんません」
lines.english: “Oh. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 店員に呼ばれて俺はふたたび歩きだした。どうでもいい。そんなことより俺が考えるべきは、二杯目のドリンクと、明日の仕事の有無だ。
lines.english: The employee's voice got me moving again. It didn't matter. I had more important things to think about: my second drink, and whether I had work tomorrow.

lines.japanese: 三つ目の角を曲がったところで、目当てのマシーンが待っていた。
lines.english: We rounded the third corner, and there stood the machine I wanted.

lines.japanese: ボタンがいっぱい付いてる。香田が言ってた通り、たしかに選択肢が豊富だ。しかも──
lines.english: Buttons everywhere. Koda hadn't been kidding; there was plenty to choose from. And then—

lines.japanese: 「おおっ」
lines.english: “Whoa.”

lines.japanese: ──味噌汁まであるじゃないか。噂をすればなんとやらだ。
lines.english: —they even had miso soup. Speak of the devil.

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょー、これマジ飲み放題いいの。マジで味噌汁すきなだけ飲んでいいの」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, seriously? This is really unlimited? I can drink all the miso soup I want?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　はあ、どうぞ」
lines.english: “What? Ah... yes, sir. Help yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。やべえな、この店。日本人の心わかりすぎだろ、天下取れるわ」
lines.english: “Seriously? This place is incredible. It understands the Japanese soul so well it could rule the country.”

lines.japanese: 俺はプチ感動した。お箸の国のひとだもの。
lines.english: I was quietly moved. I was a man from the land of chopsticks, after all.

lines.japanese: グラスをマグカップに交換して一杯注いだ。待ちきれず、その場ですこし口に含んでみる。
lines.english: I traded my glass for a mug and poured a cup. Unable to wait, I tried a little right there beside the machine.

lines.japanese: 火傷しそうなほど熱かった。
lines.english: It was hot enough to scald me.
